description: Pinned external tools for kalkan (docs/ENGINE-SPEC.md, section 12). Never install a version that is not listed here.

trivy.blocked_reason: CVE-2026-33634: compromised release builds. Never install or run them.
trivy.notes: The v0.75.0 release ships no windows-arm64 build.

gitleaks.notes: The release publishes no signature. The gitleaks GitHub Action has a separate license; kalkan uses the CLI only.

opengrep.notes: The release has no checksums file. kalkan downloaded every asset at pin time, computed its SHA-256 and compared it with the GitHub release asset digest. The v1.30.1 release ships no windows-arm64 build. The Linux assets are the manylinux (glibc) builds; musl-based systems such as Alpine are not covered.

hadolint.notes: The v2.15.1 release ships no windows-arm64 build. The release publishes no signature. kalkan runs the unmodified binary as a separate process only (GPL-3.0).

go.notes: The Go toolchain that gosec and govulncheck need. The newest stable 1.26 release on 2026-10-16 (go.dev also lists 1.27.x). Released on 2026-10-08, so the pin of 2026-10-16 was younger than the 14 days of ADR-0005: on 2026-10-25 every archive was downloaded again and its SHA-256, size, file count, tree_sha256, binary_sha256 and header matched the pinned values and the go.dev listing, and pinned_at names that day. 1.26.10 (2026-10-19) is younger than 14 days. kalkan extracts the whole archive into .tools/go/1.26.9/go (GOROOT). tree_sha256 and files were computed at pin time from the archive members (kalkan.tools.manifest.tree_digest). go.dev publishes no signature for the archives. docker/Dockerfile pins the same version and the same linux SHA-256 values. A system Go is used only when this copy is missing and its version is at least the highest min_go_version of the Go tools.

gosec.notes: gosec needs the Go toolchain at run time: kalkan puts the Go of the tool go first on PATH. min_go_version: the go directive of the gosec 2.29.0 go.mod. The Windows assets are tar.gz archives.

osv-scanner.notes: The provenance subjects match the SHA256SUMS file (checked at pin time).

grype.notes: The v0.119.0 release ships no windows-arm64 build.

checkov.notes: Installed with pip into the tool venv .tools/pyenv. Upstream classifiers list Python 3.9 to 3.12. checkov --version asks PyPI for the newest release (CONNECT pypi.org:443, measured on 2026-10-25); version_env turns that off as the adapter does.

bandit.notes: Installed with pip into the tool venv .tools/pyenv with the sarif extra.

govulncheck.notes: Built from source with go install and the Go of the tool go (GOTOOLCHAIN=local; GOPATH, GOMODCACHE and GOCACHE under .tools/go-build). The Go checksum database verifies the module. min_go_version: the go directive of the x/vuln v1.8.0 go.mod. govulncheck -version reads the modification time of its database, by default from vuln.go.dev (CONNECT vuln.go.dev:443, measured on 2026-10-25): the version probe passes -db with the file URL of its empty working folder, which govulncheck reads as an empty local database.

zizmor.notes: The assets are the PyPI wheels of zizmor 1.30.1. A wheel is a zip archive: kalkan extracts only the executable zizmor-1.30.1.data/scripts/zizmor (zizmor.exe on Windows). The SHA-256 values are the digests that PyPI publishes for the files (checksums_url). At pin time every wheel was downloaded, its SHA-256 matched the PyPI digest, the executable matched the RECORD entry of the wheel, and its header matched the platform. The wheels and not the GitHub release binaries: the Linux wheels need glibc 2.28 (x86_64) or 2.18 (aarch64), the release binaries glibc 2.34 (measured on 2026-10-25), and the release has no checksums file (its binaries carry GitHub build attestations, the wheels carry none). zizmor publishes no windows-arm64 build, neither a wheel nor a binary. The windows-arm64 asset is therefore the windows-amd64 wheel: Windows 11 on Arm runs x64 programs through its built-in emulation (not tested on Arm hardware). 1.30.1 is the newest release that was at least 14 days old on 2026-10-25 (ADR-0005); 1.31.0 and 1.31.1 (2026-10-15) are younger.

actionlint.notes: kalkan never lets actionlint start a shellcheck or pyflakes of the system: it passes -pyflakes= always and -shellcheck= unless a pinned kalkan copy of shellcheck is installed.

poutine.notes: The v1.1.6 release ships no Windows binary, so kalkan builds poutine from source on every platform: go install with the Go of the tool go (GOTOOLCHAIN=local; GOPATH, GOMODCACHE and GOCACHE under .tools/go-build). The Go checksum database verifies the module. build_flags stamp the release version and the commit of the v1.1.6 tag into the binary, as the upstream release build does; a plain go install reports the version development. -trimpath keeps the build folder out of the binary. min_go_version: the go directive of the poutine v1.1.6 go.mod. Every poutine command except mcp-server and completion sends a version check with an anonymous instance ID to version-check.cicd.fun once a day: kalkan always passes --disable-version-check (version_args too) and sets POUTINE_DISABLE_VERSION_CHECK=1.

scorecard.notes: kalkan runs scorecard --local only, with the checks that read files and need no network (docs/ENGINE-SPEC.md, section 13). The provenance subjects match the checksums file (checked at pin time). The Windows assets are tar.gz archives. 5.5.0 is the newest release that was at least 14 days old on 2026-10-25 (ADR-0005); 5.6.0 (2026-10-12) is younger.

kingfisher.notes: The release has no plain checksums file: the SHA-256 values are the subjects of the SLSA provenance multiple.intoto.jsonl, and they matched the downloads and the GitHub release asset digests at pin time. Every archive also holds a CHECKSUM file (CHECKSUM.txt or CHECKSUM-<platform>.txt) with the SHA-256 of the executable; it matches binary_sha256. 2.11.1 is the newest release that was at least 14 days old on 2026-10-25 (ADR-0005); 2.12.0 to 2.14.0 are younger. The adapter turns off the validation of found secrets against live services and the update check (docs/SECURITY.md).

shellcheck.notes: The release has no checksums file and no signature. kalkan downloaded every asset at pin time, computed its SHA-256 and compared it with the GitHub release asset digest. The release ships one Windows build, for x86_64 (shellcheck-v0.11.0.zip). windows-arm64 uses that x64 build: Windows 11 on Arm runs it through its x64 emulation. kalkan runs the unmodified binary as a separate process only (GPL-3.0).

flawfinder.notes: Installed with pip into the tool venv .tools/pyenv (pure Python, no dependencies). kalkan runs it unmodified as a separate process only (GPL-2.0-or-later).

gixy.notes: The maintained fork of yandex/gixy (PyPI gixy-ng). Its LICENSE file is the Mozilla Public License 2.0 with two copyright lines in front of it, so the GitHub metadata says NOASSERTION. Installed with pip into the tool venv .tools/pyenv without the deep extra: its dependencies are ngxparse (Apache-2.0), Jinja2 and MarkupSafe (BSD-3-Clause) and ConfigArgParse (MIT). kalkan does not use the release binaries: they bundle redoctor (checked in the 0.2.55 Windows binary), whose Business Source License 1.1 allows production use for non-commercial purposes only (not OSI-approved). pip also covers darwin-amd64 and windows-arm64, which have no release binary. 0.2.55 is the newest release that was at least 14 days old on 2026-10-25 (ADR-0005); 0.2.57 (2026-10-20) and 0.2.58 (2026-10-25) are younger.

helm.notes: Helm 4.3.0 (2026-09-09) is the newest stable release published on or before 2026-10-11 (ADR-0005 rule 1); 4.3.1 and 3.22.1 came out on 2026-10-15. Helm 3 gets no new minor release and reaches its end of life (helm.sh/blog/helm-v3-end-of-life), so the 4.x line is pinned. Helm publishes its binaries on get.helm.sh, not as GitHub release assets: every asset has its own checksum file <asset url>.sha256sum (checksums_url names the linux-amd64 one), and the GitHub release notes list the same SHA-256 values. At pin time all six downloads matched both, and the PGP signature <asset>.asc of each archive (GitHub release asset) verified with the release key 208D D36E D5BB 3745 A167 43A4 C7C6 FBB5 B91C 1155 of the KEYS file of the tag. kalkan uses helm only to render charts offline with helm template (helm-checkov adapter, docs/ENGINE-SPEC.md section 13): never dependency update or build, no repository, no --repo, and HELM_CACHE_HOME, HELM_CONFIG_HOME and HELM_DATA_HOME in the work folder.

vacuum.notes: vacuum 0.33.0 (2026-10-10) is the newest stable release published on or before 2026-10-11 (ADR-0005 rule 1); 0.33.1 followed on 2026-10-15. The sigstore bundle signs checksums.txt (identity: the publish workflow of the main branch, not of the tag). The Windows assets are tar.gz archives. kalkan runs vacuum spectral-report with --remote=false, --no-update-check, its own ruleset (the built-in OWASP rules) and an empty config file, and only on specifications whose local references stay inside the target (docs/ENGINE-SPEC.md section 13, docs/SECURITY.md).
